name: bayes-group-website
summary: Marketing website for The Bayes Group built with Vite, React, TypeScript, React Router and plain CSS using design‑tokens (CSS custom properties).
steps: 1. Run `npm create vite@latest bayes-group-website -- --template react-ts` to scaffold a Vite + React + TypeScript project.
2. Add runtime dependencies: `npm i react-router-dom` and dev dependencies for testing: `npm i -D @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom jest ts-jest @types/jest`.
3. In `vite.config.ts` set `base: './'` so the build produces a relative `dist/index.html`.

4. Create `src/index.css` that defines design‑token CSS custom properties for colors (`--color-primary: #0B1F3A; --color-accent: #1F8A8A; --color-bg: #ffffff;`), font stacks (serif for headings, system sans‑serif for body), and whitespace (grid gaps, container width). Include a global `box‑sizing: border-box` reset and responsive breakpoints.

5. Build a `Wordmark` component (`src/components/Wordmark.tsx`) that returns an inline SVG: a minimal bell‑curve shape followed by the text "The Bayes Group". Export it for reuse in header and footer.
6. Implement `Header` (`src/components/Header.tsx`) containing:
- The `Wordmark` linking to `/`.
- A `<nav>` with links to `/services`, `/training`, `/about`, `/contact` and a "Book a consultation" `<button>` linking to `/contact`.
- A responsive "Menu" button that appears when `window.innerWidth < 420px`. Clicking it toggles a collapsible list of the navigation links.
- Semantic landmarks: `<header>` and `<nav>`.
7. Implement `Footer` (`src/components/Footer.tsx`) containing:
- The `Wordmark` (non‑link).
- The tagline line "AI enablement, training and custom development.".
- The same navigation links as the header.
- Copyright text `© 2026 The Bayes Group`.
- Semantic `<footer>` landmark.
8. Create `src/App.tsx` that wraps the app in `<BrowserRouter>` and renders a `<Header/>`, a `<main>` with `<Routes>` for:
- `/services` → `Services`
- `/training` → `Training`
- `/about` → `About`
- `/contact` → `Contact`
- `*` → `NotFound`
The `NotFound` page displays an h1 "Page not found" and a link back to home.
After each navigation, a `useEffect` sets `document.title` to the page‑specific title (e.g. "Services | The Bayes Group").
9. Build `Home` page (`src/pages/Home.tsx`) with:
- An `<h1>` containing "Evidence-driven AI, built for your business.".
- A hero section with a one‑sentence value proposition and two `<a>` buttons ("Book a consultation" → `/contact`, "Explore services" → `/services`).

- Three pillar cards for "AI Enablement", "Training", "Custom Development" each with descriptive text and a "Learn more" link pointing to the appropriate anchor on `/services` (`/services#enablement`, etc.).
- A "How we work" section with four numbered steps (Assess, Design, Build, Enable) and a short sentence each.
- A "Why The Bayes Group" section with four bullet points describing the team’s credentials, hands‑on building, vendor‑neutral advice, and knowledge transfer.
- A call‑to‑action band with the tagline "Ready to put AI to work?" and a "Book a consultation" button linking to `/contact`.
10. Build `Services` page (`src/pages/Services.tsx`):
- `<h1>` "Services".
- Three sections with ids `enablement`, `training`, `custom-development` in that order.
- Each section lists the items described in the specification (name + one‑sentence description).
- Each section ends with a line "Typical engagement: X to Y weeks" (e.g. "Typical engagement: 2 to 6 weeks").
11. Build `Training` page (`src/pages/Training.tsx`):
- `<h1>` "Training".
- A static array of at least six course objects containing `title`, `audience` ("Executives" | "Managers" | "Technical teams"), `format`, `duration`, and a three‑item `learn` list.
- Four filter buttons: All, Executives, Managers, Technical teams. The selected button has `aria-pressed="true"` and a distinct visual style.
- Clicking a filter updates displayed course cards to only those matching the audience; "All" shows every course.
- Each course card displays the required fields.
12. Build `About` page (`src/pages/About.tsx`):
- `<h1>` "About".
- Mission paragraph and a "Why Bayes" paragraph (including the Bayesian reasoning line).
- Two founder cards with placeholder content (`name: "Founder Name"`, `role: "Co‑founder & Principal Data Scientist"`, placeholder credentials list, placeholder bio).
- Four value statements: Evidence over hype; Build to transfer; Vendor‑neutral; Responsible by design.
13. Build `Contact` page (`src/pages/Contact.tsx`):
- `<h1>` "Book a consultation".
- Display the email `hello@thebayesgroup.com`.

- A form with labelled inputs: Name (required), Email (required, valid email), Company (optional), a `<select>` named "What can we help with?" with the four options, and a textarea Message (required).
- Client‑side validation: on submit, if a required field is empty or Email is invalid, render the exact error messages next to the field:
* "Please enter your name."
* "Please enter a valid email address."
* "Please enter a message."
- No network request is made; on successful validation replace the form with the success text: "Thanks, we'll be in touch within one business day." and clear the form fields.
14. Build `NotFound` page (`src/pages/NotFound.tsx`):
- `<h1>` "Page not found".
- A link back to the home page (`/`).
15. Write responsive CSS (in `src/index.css` or component‑scoped CSS) that:
- Prevents horizontal scrolling at 390 px width and 1440 px width.
- Collapses the header navigation into a "Menu" button on small screens (≤ 420 px).
- Uses the deep navy (`#0B1F3A`) as primary background/text color, white for contrast, and teal (`#1F8A8A`) as the accent for buttons, links, and highlights.
- Applies the serif font stack to all `<h1>`‑`<h4>` elements and a system sans‑serif stack to body text, ensuring WCAG AA contrast.
16. Ensure every page contains exactly one `<h1>` element (asserted in tests).
17. Add `aria-pressed` handling on filter buttons and make focus outlines visible for keyboard navigation.
18. Verify the build script `npm run build` outputs a `dist/index.html` that can be served statically.
19. Add a `README.md` (optional) explaining how to run `npm install`, `npm run dev`, and `npm run build`.

acceptance_files.test_acceptance.py:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Runs the app's acceptance tests: the Jest files in __tests__/acceptance/. Generated by the pipeline; the tests
themselves are locked files written by the planner. ACCEPTANCE_MILESTONE=N runs only the tests of milestones 1..N."""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
os.chdir(here)
if not os.path.isdir("node_modules"):
    lock = os.path.exists("package-lock.json")
    subprocess.run(["npm", "ci" if lock else "install", "--include=dev", "--no-audit", "--no-fund"], check=False, timeout=1500)
cmd = ["npx", "jest", "--ci", "__tests__/acceptance"]
m = os.environ.get("ACCEPTANCE_MILESTONE", "")
if m.isdigit():
    cmd += ["-t", "^(" + "|".join("M%d" % i for i in range(1, int(m) + 1)) + "): "]
# The app's own test script may add node flags (e.g. --experimental-vm-modules): use the same ones.
try:
    script = json.load(open("package.json")).get("scripts", {}).get("test", "")
except (OSError, ValueError):
    script = ""
env = dict(os.environ)
if "--experimental-vm-modules" in script:
    env["NODE_OPTIONS"] = (env.get("NODE_OPTIONS", "") + " --experimental-vm-modules").strip()
print("Running: " + " ".join(cmd), flush=True)
sys.exit(subprocess.run(cmd, env=env, timeout=1500).returncode)

requirements.text: The site must be built with Vite, React, TypeScript and react-router.
Styling must be plain CSS using a design‑token theme with CSS custom properties.
Running `npm run build` must produce a `dist/index.html` file.
The site must be a static site with no backend, no user accounts, no analytics, no third‑party scripts, and no external font or image CDNs.
The overall color palette must be deep navy (#0B1F3A), white, and teal (#1F8A8A) as an accent.
Headings must use a serif system‑font stack; body text must use a clean sans‑serif system‑font stack.
The wordmark logo must be an inline SVG consisting of a small bell‑curve graphic followed by the text "The Bayes Group".
The site must be responsive from 390 px wide (phone) to 1440 px wide (desktop) and never scroll horizontally.
On screens ≤ 390 px wide the header navigation must collapse into a "Menu" button that toggles the visibility of the navigation links.
Every page must contain the same header with the wordmark linking to "/", navigation links to Services, Training, About, Contact, and a "Book a consultation" button linking to "/contact".
Every page must contain the same footer with the wordmark, the line "AI enablement, training and custom development.", the navigation links, and the copyright text "© 2026 The Bayes Group".
Each page must set its document.title according to the specification (e.g., "Services | The Bayes Group", home title "The Bayes Group | Evidence-driven AI").
Each page must contain exactly one <h1> element.
Home page hero must display an <h1> with the text "Evidence-driven AI, built for your business."
Home page hero must contain a value‑proposition sentence and two buttons: "Book a consultation" linking to "/contact" and "Explore services" linking to "/services".
Home page must show three pillar cards titled "AI Enablement", "Training", and "Custom Development", each with two‑or‑three sentences and a "Learn more" link to the appropriate anchor on /services.
Home page must include a "How we work" section with four numbered steps (Assess, Design, Build, Enable) each with one sentence.
Home page must include a "Why The Bayes Group" section with four points: credentialed data scientists, hands‑on builders, vendor‑neutral advice, knowledge transfer so your team owns the result.
Home page must end with a call‑to‑action band containing the text "Ready to put AI to work?" and a "Book a consultation" button linking to "/contact".
Services page must have an <h1> with the text "Services".
Services page must contain three sections with ids "enablement", "training", and "custom-development" in that order.
Enablement section must list: AI readiness assessment; use‑case discovery and prioritization; AI strategy and roadmap; AI governance and responsible‑AI policy.
Training section must list: executive AI briefings; hands‑on team workshops; deep‑learning bootcamps for technical teams; custom curricula.

Custom development section must list: LLM and retrieval‑augmented (RAG) applications; AI agents and workflow automation; predictive models and ML pipelines; deep‑learning solutions; integration with existing systems.
Each item in the Services lists must display its name and a one‑sentence description.
Each Services subsection must end with a line showing the typical engagement duration (e.g., "2 to 6 weeks").
Training page must have an <h1> with the text "Training".
Training page must display at least six course cards.

Each course card must show the course title, audience (exactly one of: Executives, Managers, Technical teams), format (Half‑day briefing, 1‑day workshop or Multi‑week bootcamp), duration, and a "You will learn" list of three items.
Training page must have four filter buttons labeled All, Executives, Managers, Technical teams.
When the Training page loads, the "All" filter button must be selected by default and all course cards must be visible.
Selecting a filter button must display only the courses whose audience matches the selected filter.
The selected filter button must be visibly marked and have attribute aria-pressed="true".
About page must have an <h1> with the text "About".
About page must contain a mission paragraph and a "Why Bayes" paragraph with the specified content about Bayesian reasoning.
About page must display two founder cards with placeholder content: name "Founder Name", role "Co‑founder & Principal Data Scientist", a credentials list, and a short bio, all marked as placeholders.
About page must list four values: Evidence over hype; Build to transfer; Vendor‑neutral; Responsible by design.
Contact page must have an <h1> with the text "Book a consultation".
Contact page must display the email address hello@thebayesgroup.com.

Contact page must contain a form with labelled fields: Name, Email, Company, "What can we help with?" (select with options AI Enablement, Training, Custom Development, Not sure yet), and Message, plus a "Send message" button.
Form fields Name, Email and Message must be required.
Email field must validate that the input is a syntactically valid email address.

On submit, if a required field is empty or Email is invalid, an error message must appear next to the field with the exact text: "Please enter your name.", "Please enter a valid email address.", or "Please enter a message.", respectively.

When the form is submitted with all required fields valid, no network request must be performed, a success message "Thanks, we'll be in touch within one business day." must be shown, and the form fields must be cleared.
Any unknown route must render a page with an <h1> "Page not found" and a link back to the home page.
Each page must include semantic landmarks: <header>, <nav>, <main>, and <footer>.
Every form field must have an associated <label> element.
Keyboard focus indicators must be visible for all interactive elements.
All text must meet WCAG AA contrast ratios against the background.
